'''Thomas Israel Banks'''<ref>{{Cite web |title=Physics Tree - Thomas Israel Banks |url=https://academictree.org/physics/peopleinfo.php?pid=594949 |access-date=2022-11-20 |website=academictree.org}}</ref> (born April 19,<ref>''[[American Men and Women of Science]]'', 21st ed., 2009, p. 318.</ref> 1949 in New York City<ref>[http://library.ias.edu/files/pdfs/ar/annualreportforf1984inst.pdf ''The Institute for Advanced Study. Annual Report 1983/84''], p. 55.</ref>) is a theoretical physicist and professor at [[Rutgers University]] and [[University of California, Santa Cruz]].

==Work==
Banks' work centers around [[string theory]] and its applications to high energy particle physics and cosmology. He received his Ph.D. in physics from the [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]] in 1973. From 1973 to 1977 he was a post doctorate at [[Tel Aviv University]] and stayed on first as a lecturer and then as a professor until 1986.<ref>{{Cite web |title=CV |url=http://scipp.ucsc.edu/personnel/profiles/banks/Banks_2012.pdf |access-date=2022-11-20}}</ref> He was several times a visiting scholar at the [[Institute for Advanced Study]] in Princeton (1976–78, 1983–84, 2010).<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.ias.edu/scholars/thomas-banks|title=Thomas Banks|website=Institute for Advanced Study|language=en|access-date=2018-12-25}}</ref>

Along with [[Willy Fischler]], [[Stephen Shenker]], and [[Leonard Susskind]], he is one of the four originators of [[Matrix theory (physics)|M(atrix) theory]], or BFSS Matrix Theory, an attempt to formulate [[M theory]] in a [[Non-perturbative|nonperturbative]] manner. Banks proposed a conjecture known as [[asymptotic darkness]]—it posits that the physics above the [[Planck scale]] is dominated by black hole production. He has often criticized the widely held assumption in the string theory community that background spacetimes with different asymptotics can represent different vacua states of the same theory of quantum gravity. Rather, Banks argues that different asymptotics correspond to different models of quantum gravity.<ref>Banks, Tom [https://arxiv.org/abs/1007.4001v3 "TASI Lectures on Holographic Space-Time, SUSY and Gravitational Effective Field Theory"], 2010, p. 9.</ref> Many of his arguments for this and other ideas are contained in his paper "A Critique of Pure String Theory: Heterodox Opinions of Diverse Dimensions." published in 2003.<ref>Banks, Tom [https://arxiv.org/abs/hep-th/0306074v1 "A Critique of Pure String Theory: Heterodox Opinions of Diverse Dimensions."], 2003.</ref>
